title: Persistent Prayer, the Rich Ruler, and Blind Bartimaeus

questions.question: Jesus told them a parable to the effect that they ought always to pray and not lose heart. It concerned a judge in a certain city who neither feared God nor respected man. Who kept coming to him?
options: A widow, saying, "Give me justice against my adversary."
A young orphan begging for bread daily
A tax collector seeking asylum from the crowd
A priest who was robbed on the road
questions.correctAnswer: A widow, saying, "Give me justice against my adversary."
questions.explanation: Luke 18:3 (ESV): "And there was a widow in that city who kept coming to him and saying, 'Give me justice against my adversary.'"

questions.question: Why did the unrighteous judge finally decide to give the widow justice?
options: Because this widow keeps bothering him, so that she will not beat him down by her continual coming
Because he finally feared the judgment of God upon him
Because the townspeople pressured him to change
Because she paid a small bribe constantly over time
questions.correctAnswer: Because this widow keeps bothering him, so that she will not beat him down by her continual coming
questions.explanation: Luke 18:4-5 (ESV): "yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will give her justice, so that she will not beat me down by her continual coming."

questions.question: Jesus ends the parable of the persistent widow with a sobering question: "Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find..."?
options: "...faith on earth?"
"...prayers ascending to heaven?"
"...patience among the saints?"
"...justice in the courts of men?"
questions.explanation: Luke 18:8 (ESV): "I tell you, he will give justice to them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth?"

questions.question: There was a Pharisee and a tax collector who went up into the temple to pray. In the Pharisee's prayer, for what did he thank God?
options: "That I am not like other men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector."
"That I have been given the wisdom to understand the Law fully."
"That my family has been healthy throughout the cold winter."
"That the offerings I bring are twice as heavy as the others."
questions.correctAnswer: "That I am not like other men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector."
questions.explanation: Luke 18:11 (ESV): "The Pharisee, standing by himself, prayed thus: 'God, I thank you that I am not like other men, extortioners, unjust... or even like this tax collector.'"

questions.question: What did the tax collector do while praying in the temple?
options: He stood far off, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, "God, be merciful to me, a sinner!"
He laid prostrate on the stone floor for seven hours weeping loudly
He read the penitential Psalms continuously from memory
He washed his hands and feet slowly at the bronze basin first
questions.correctAnswer: He stood far off, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, "God, be merciful to me, a sinner!"
questions.explanation: Luke 18:13 (ESV): "But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, 'God, be merciful to me, a sinner!'"

questions.question: Jesus declared that the tax collector went down to his house justified, rather than the Pharisee. Why?
options: "For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted."
"For true tithing involves the heart and not the purse."
"Because repentance cannot be spoken aloud in pride."
"Heaven only listens to the poor and rejected."
questions.correctAnswer: "For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted."
questions.explanation: Luke 18:14 (ESV): "I tell you, this man went down to his house justified, rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted."

questions.question: When people brought infants to Jesus and the disciples rebuked them, Jesus called them and said, "Let the children come to me... for to such belongs the kingdom of God." He added that whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like what shall not enter it?
options: Like a child
Like a dove
Like a fine grain of sand
Like pure water
questions.explanation: Luke 18:17 (ESV): "Truly, I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child shall not enter it."

questions.question: A ruler asked, "Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?" How did Jesus respond first to his greeting?
options: "Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone."
"There is none good but the prophets who suffer in truth."
"You flatter me, yet your heart remains distant."
"Only the law is perfectly good, therefore keep it from your youth."
questions.correctAnswer: "Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone."
questions.explanation: Luke 18:19 (ESV): "And Jesus said to him, 'Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.'"

questions.question: The ruler said he had kept all the commandments from his youth. Jesus told him he still lacked one thing. What was he instructed to do?
options: "Sell all that you have and distribute to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me."
"Give half of your wealth to the temple and fast forty days."
"Leave your family behind and preach the gospel in Samaria."
"Free your servants immediately, and cancel all your debts."
questions.correctAnswer: "Sell all that you have and distribute to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me."
questions.explanation: Luke 18:22 (ESV): "When Jesus heard this, he said to him, 'One thing you still lack. Sell all that you have and distribute to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.'"

questions.question: Why did the ruler become very sad upon hearing this?
options: For he was extremely rich
For he loved his many comfortable mansions
For his family would mock him fiercely
For he feared life in the dusty streets
questions.explanation: Luke 18:23 (ESV): "But when he heard these things, he became very sad, for he was extremely rich."

questions.question: Seeing the ruler sad, Jesus remarked how difficult it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God. What analogy did He use?
options: "For it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
"For it is easier to empty the sea with a broken cup than for a rich man to change entirely."
"For a lion will sooner lay with a lamb than a rich man surrender all his gold."
"It is as difficult as moving Mount Hermon with a single word."
questions.correctAnswer: "For it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
questions.explanation: Luke 18:25 (ESV): "For it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."

questions.question: Hearing this, those who were listening asked, "Then who can be saved?" What did Jesus reply? (Luke 18:27)
options: "What is impossible with man is possible with God."
"The poorest beggar is already saved today."
"Only those who fast completely and never fail in faith."
"With pain and suffering, the few will enter safely."
questions.correctAnswer: "What is impossible with man is possible with God."
questions.explanation: Luke 18:27 (ESV): "But he said, 'What is impossible with man is possible with God.'"

questions.question: Taking the twelve, Jesus predicted His death and resurrection for the third time in Luke. He explained that everything written about the Son of Man by the prophets will be accomplished. Did the disciples understand this?
options: But they understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them
They understood fully and wept bitterly together
Peter understood partially and was angered by the news
They cheered because he said he would rise on the third day
questions.correctAnswer: But they understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them
questions.explanation: Luke 18:34 (ESV): "But they understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what was said."

questions.question: As Jesus drew near to Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the roadside begging. Hearing the crowd, he found out it was Jesus of Nazareth passing by. What did he constantly cry out?
options: "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
"Master, Holy One of God, open my eyes!"
"Prophet of Galilee, hear my lament!"
"Lord of the Sabbath, rescue me from the dark!"
questions.correctAnswer: "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
questions.explanation: Luke 18:38 (ESV): "And he cried out, 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!'"

questions.question: When the preceding crowd rebuked the blind man, telling him to be silent, what did he do?
options: He cried out all the more
He fell silent but wept heavily
He stood up and cursed them loudly
He tried to grab onto their cloaks desperate to find him
questions.correctAnswer: He cried out all the more
questions.explanation: Luke 18:39 (ESV): "And those who were in front rebuked him, telling him to be silent. But he cried out all the more, 'Son of David, have mercy on me!'"

key_verse_text: But he said, "What is impossible with man is possible with God."
